raw_response:
I farm 10.1 mu, and I have done wheat-maize for many years, so I will still follow that road this year. I do not like changing too much at once. Around me, if wheat wants a steady stand and good ears, I have to put the base fertilizer down solid, and with maize I cannot let it run short on fertilizer during the jointing and tasseling time. I studied to middle school, so I do look at the field condition, not only at habit. My land has well irrigation, so I am less afraid of dry weather than people who wait only for rain. Since my family has only 2 people and some labor goes off-farm, I will keep the work simple and practical: improved seed, rotary tillage, enough fertilizer, a few key irrigations, and pesticide only at the main risk times. Fertilizer costs money, that is true, but if I save too hard and lose yield, that loss is bigger. So for wheat I will keep nitrogen a bit higher and give 3 irrigations if the weather is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, enough nitrogen, and 2 irrigations with topdressing. Yield is what pays the year, so I will spend on the main inputs first and not gamble on cutting them too much.
